problems.stem: A ten-day asynchronous storyboard sprint has a single milestone: upload the finished storyboard on Day 10. Which change best facilitates the distributed cohort?
options: Move the single deadline later so students have more total time.
Add a Day 3 three-frame skeleton and a Day 6 signaling pass that post to a shared thread, keeping the Day 10 final.
Schedule one mandatory live critique that all four time zones must attend.
Tell students to upload whenever the storyboard looks polished.
problems.explanation: Distributing checkpoints lets stalled storyboards surface early instead of all design reasoning bursting at one deadline.

problems.stem: A student in the async studio is stuck. Which stuck-note lets the instructor reply with targeted help?
options: Frame 4: I cannot decide whether the narration should name the learner action before or after the on-screen prompt.
I am behind on the sprint.
Can you look at my work?
problems.explanation: Pinning the note to one frame and one unresolved decision lets the reply target that frame instead of the whole artifact.

problems.stem: Two storyboards stall by Day 4. What is the strongest asynchronous facilitation move?
options: Call an emergency synchronous session that all four time zones must join.
Reply asynchronously to each stalled student's tagged frame with one targeted prompt within 24 hours.
Wait until the Day 10 deadline to see if they recover on their own.
Lower the requirements so the stalled storyboards still pass.
problems.explanation: Asynchronous facilitation relies on visible artifacts and targeted async support, not a synchronous fallback that excludes off-hours learners.

problems.stem: The instructor wants evidence that the added checkpoints actually improved facilitation. Which comparison shows it?
options: The Day 10 storyboards look more polished than last term's.
Stalled storyboards were caught on Day 4 with checkpoints versus only on Day 10 without them.
More students submitted in the final 36 hours.
The total page count of the storyboards increased.
problems.explanation: The auditable evidence is the earlier detection of stalled work that the distributed checkpoints made possible.
